outline.description: Sets the stage by tracing the evolution of sequence models from early recurrent networks through Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to modern Transformer architectures. It explains why revisiting LSTMs is interesting despite the dominance of Transformers, introduces the central research question addressed by the paper, and outlines the main contributions of xLSTM.
subtopics: Historical timeline of sequence modeling architectures
Key successes of classical LSTMs across domains
Rise of Transformer models and their advantages
Limitations prompting a re-examination of recurrent models
Research question: performance limits when scaling LSTMs

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Recurrent Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory
outline.description: Provides the mathematical background needed to understand later extensions. Covers basic recurrent network formulation, gradient propagation through time, vanishing/exploding gradients problem, and the original LSTM design with its constant error carousel.
subtopics: Gradient stability issues in vanilla RNNs
- Cell state update c_t = f_t c_{t-1} + i_t z_t
- Role of peephole connections and multi-cell vectors
Interpretation of the constant error carousel
Empirical impact of gated recurrence in early NLP tasks
